title: Operator Edge Onboarding Checklist and Audit Walkthrough
summary: Practical operator-facing checklist and conversational walkthrough for customer-managed edge/VPC onboarding. Emphasizes compact audit payloads, deterministic approval tokens, and a two-mode telemetry model (sparse vs. forensic) to reduce data egress while preserving verifiability.
audience: Solutions Engineers, Oncall SREs, Customer Onboarding Operators, Product Managers
prerequisites: Customer assigned technical contact and maintenance window
Network pre-check completed (IP ranges, NAT rules, BGP/peering summary)
Customer capability: provide KMS public key or HSM handshake endpoint
Ticket created in JIRA and linked to customer account
operator-checklist-compact: Contact validation: confirm contact phone + slack channel
Key exchange: request base64-wrapped public key or configure HSM URL
Telemetry mode: choose 'sparse' (default) or 'forensic' per customer compliance
Approval token: generate one-hour approval token and request customer sign-off
Apply in dry-run: ./onboard edge --dry-run --token <tok> (capture step hashes)
Post-apply smoke: run inference-smoke-check and connectivity-report
Finalize: mark onboarding complete in console; archive compact audit bundle
interactive-walkthrough-notes: Design intent: keep operator prompts minimal; prefer defaults for common enterprise combos
UX friction seen in pilots: customers struggle to produce HSM endpoint cert chains; add short helper script to extract chain
Recommendation: auto-generate example approval email template from CLI to reduce back-and-forth
Edge cases: intermittent peering flaps require retry loop with exponential backoff and a single visible retry counter in CLI output
runbook-examples-and-commands:
# Net verify sample output:
CONTROL_PLANE: 3/3 reachable
median_rtt_ms: 14
candidate_route: cust-cidr -> cp-zone-a (peering)

# Approval token flow (CLI):
$ ./onboard edge --generate-approval --customer-id CUST123
APPROVAL_TOKEN: apr_2026_01_05_14h
valid_for: 01:00:00
log_ref: audit:apr_2026_01_05_14h.hash

# Dry-run streaming log (truncated):
[DRYRUN] STEP: install-edge-agent -> OK
[DRYRUN] STEP: configure-firewall -> OK
[DRYRUN] CHECKPOINT: sha256:2b7f... (store in bundle)

# Apply streaming log (truncated):
[APPLY] STEP: attach-route-table -> OK
[APPLY] STEP: register-agent -> OK
[APPLY] FINAL_CHECKSUM: sha256:d4c1...

# Compact audit bundle structure (human-readable summary):
- manifest.txt (operator, customer, timestamp, approval_token_id)
- step_hashes.txt (ordered sha256 per step)
- generated_signatures.txt (operator signature + optional customer ack)

# Smoke test sample (CLI):
$ ./inference-smoke --endpoint <edge>
model_ping: ok
median_latency_ms: 42
token_success_rate: 99.6%
rollback-playbook: Trigger criteria: failed smoke tests OR customer reports critical connectivity failure
Immediate: run ./onboard edge --rollback --bundle <bundle_id> to revert agent registration and firewall changes
Forensic capture: collect live snapshot (sparse) and store in temp-forensics bucket with short TTL
Communication: notify customer of rollback with summary of step_hashes and expected remediation timeline
Postmortem: create a JIRA postmortem ticket linking audit bundle and operator notes
sparse-vs-forensic-telemetry-guidance: Sparse mode (default): capture step-level checksums, control-plane reachability, final_checksum, and minimal error samples; retention 30 days
Forensic mode (on request): include wire-level nettraces, verbose container logs for 72 hours, and full step stdout; retention 90 days and requires explicit customer consent
Storage note: compact audit bundles are signed and immutable; large forensic captures are stored separately and only referenced in compact manifest
Privacy note: redact customer PII from logs prior to long-term archival unless customer contract permits
open-questions-and-risks: How should we model multi-operator approvals (2-of-3 witness) in the minimal approval token UX?
What is acceptable default retention for compact bundles for enterprise customers with strict audit needs?
Risk: customers may be uncomfortable uploading HSM chain; need to provide clear helper and fallback with operator attestation
Edge-case: partial apply that leaves route tables in an inconsistent state; require idempotent apply and an inspect command
